# Predicate Index

**English** · [Chinese](predicate-index.zh-CN.md)

The place to look up "does this fact already have a predicate?" — before you write a constant, a threshold, a tolerance, a sampler, or a formatter.

## Why this page exists

`CLAUDE.md`'s first hard rule is the **shared-predicate rule**: analysis code (`packages/analysis`) and the verification gates (`packages/eval`) must decide **the same fact** with **the same predicate** — same constant, same sampling function, same tolerance — anchored on the _rendered_ value, because the gates re-parse the rendered prompt text. The rule also states the remedy: export the predicate in one place and import it on both sides; when that is impossible, write a unit test that asserts equality — do not rely on a comment.

The historical cost of breaking it: in the 2026-07 full-corpus audit, **five independent bugs were all this one class** — inconsistent HP sample radius, bounded vs unbounded backtracking, interpolated vs raw vs off-instant sampling for line of sight, and fractional seconds vs the rendered-second scan grid.

The rule was never the missing piece. On 2026-08-01 the same person, having read the rule, re-implemented two predicates by hand inside a single day's work: the "match already known" test was copied into the orchestration shell, and `dateKey` formatting was written out a second time in another file. **What was missing is an index** — somewhere to see, before writing new code, that the fact already has an owner.

## How to use it

**Before writing new code.** Search the table for the _fact_, in words — not for a symbol name you half-remember. If the fact is listed, import the predicate. Do not re-derive it, do not copy the literal, do not inline "just this once" a regex that already exists.

**When you add an "analysis asserts X, the gate verifies X" pair:**

1. Export the predicate from one module and import it on both sides.
2. Add a row to the index below — in **both** language versions.
3. Add the same row to `packages/eval/test/predicateIndex.test.ts`. That test parses this page, so the page and the test cannot rot apart.
4. If sharing the export is genuinely impossible — the other side is a markdown spec, a rendered string, or a different language — add an equality assertion to that same test. That is CLAUDE.md's explicit fallback, and a comment is not a substitute for it. `FACT_AUDIT_MIN` / `FACT_AUDIT_MAX` below is the worked example.

**When you rename or delete a predicate.** The test imports every symbol listed here, by file path. A rename breaks CI; update this page in both languages instead of deleting the row.

## Reading the table

- **Fact** — what gets decided, in words. This is the column to search.
- **Authoritative predicate** — `file` → `export`. Exactly one per fact.
- **Consumed by** — notable call sites, not an exhaustive list. "gate" means `packages/eval`.
- **Notes** — the semantics that are easy to get wrong.

Paths are relative to the repository root. Everything under `packages/analysis/src` can be imported by file path; most of it is also re-exported from the package root (`@gladlog/analysis`), but `factFormat.ts`, `spellCategories.ts`'s `isCastBlockingAuraType` and a few others are reachable only by file path.

**Scope.** The rule the index serves is "one fact, one predicate", and that is not confined to the analysis/gate pair. A fact decided by two consumers _inside_ the desktop renderer — a number the leaderboard prints and a bar the chart next to it draws — fails the same way and belongs here too (the `desktop-dev` skill calls this the UI edition of the rule). The `Report UI` section below is that case; everything else is analysis-authoritative.

| Which `SWING_DAMAGE_LANDED` line and which `SWING_DAMAGE` line are the same swing — so one swing is one damage event, carrying what landed | `packages/parser/src/l3/swingTwins.ts` → `swingLandedTwins` (window: `SWING_TWIN_WINDOW_MS`) | parser `l3/collect.ts`'s `collectEvents` (the victim-side LANDED line with damage landed IS the swing's damage event; a SWING_DAMAGE line stands in only when it has no twin); gate `packages/eval/scripts/swingLandedScan.ts` (raw-vs-parsed scan: MISSING / DOUBLE / MISMATCH / ZERO-NOABS, each must be 0) | FT-T01 + FT-T02, 2026-10-08/09. A swing is logged as `SWING_DAMAGE` (attacker's advanced block) and / or `SWING_DAMAGE_LANDED` (victim's). (1) *A lone LANDED line is a swing.* A guardian the logging client has no owner for (Unholy's Lesser Ghoul, unit flags 0xa28) writes the LANDED line only. The old rule dropped every LANDED line: on the 60 raw logs of the 2026-10-08 re-eval 5,767 swings / 3,943,822 damage never reached `damageIn` (3,845,965 of it on players; two killing blows, 06bb9860 and 7d1f14af) → 0. (2) *The victim-side line says what landed.* The two lines disagree on `amount` / `absorbed` in 1,501 of 48,537 pairs; on the 1,494 with a health reading before the hit the victim's health moved by the LANDED amount 1,494 times and by the SWING_DAMAGE amount 0 times (`fix-FT/scripts/t02_pair_truth.py`). Keeping the attacker side had 1,501 swings carry the wrong amount (1,408,728 apart in total, net +204,918), 120 of them damage the victim-side line says never landed (334,984 — counted again as their SPELL_ABSORBED) → 0. Twins = same source, same target, same `baseAmount` (the one field both sides share), nearest line first (ties in log order), within 1 s: all 48,537 pairs lie within 451 ms and no candidate exists between 452 ms and 3 s. A LANDED line with amount 0 (absorbed whole; 10,915 lines) is NOT a damage event: its absorb is its SPELL_ABSORBED record, which the scan's ZERO-NOABS class checks line by line (0 of 10,915). A melee damage event's `eventName` is therefore `SWING_DAMAGE_LANDED` almost always — a reader that enumerates event names must admit it (`externalDamage.ts`'s `DIRECT_EVENTS`). A parser drop or a wrong side is invisible to the prompt gates — they read the parser's own output — so the check is a raw-level scan, not a `check*` class. |

Until then it left out a bar with a SPELL_CAST_FAILED of the spell before its end row (`earlierFailure`, the key pressed again while the bar ran) and a completion logged after the next bar began (`queued`). 605-match capture: 126 of 1,869 kick-eaten rows change a cast-control fact (`yourCancels`, `yourCancelMedianPct`, `baitedKicks`, `baitedThisKickerT`, `stoppedJustBefore`); no row added or removed, no context line changed. **FT I11 (2026-10-11)**: two stops the player did not choose were cancels. (1) A bar the owner's own death ended: dying breaks a cast bar and the client writes the same "Interrupted" row for it — 0fe0e2e2: Sleep Walk begun 43.158, the row 43.715, the owner's UNIT_DIED 43.739 (24 ms later; 14 ms in 3b56ac97 round 6). `castBarOutcomesOf` now says `near: "death"` for a stop within `CANCEL_CC_NEAR_S` of the unit's death, beside `cc` and `displaced` — the same nearness, no constant added. (2) A bar stopped at or after the round's end (`roundEndMs`: a Solo Shuffle round is over at its first player death and the log runs on ~2 s) — f0a10402 round 3: the round-ending death 103.983, the owner's Mind Control begun 104.062, "Interrupted" 104.602. A cancel is `isCancelInRound`: `stopped`, `near === null`, the stop row before the round's end — the one test of the ledger and of the `[CAST STOPPED]` line that reads "not kicked; no control …". The kicked-by-somebody-else case was checked and is not counted: a SPELL_INTERRUPT of the bar's spell is read before its "Interrupted" row (0 of 60 cancels on five logs have an interrupt on the owner within 0.5 s). On the 605-file capture's text, of 986 `[CAST STOPPED]` cancel lines (controls only): 3 stopped in the second of the owner's own death, 17 in the second of — or after — a Solo Shuffle round's ending death; the whole-second grid cannot say which of those are the round's last real cancels, and the ledger's count over every cast-time spell needs a capture. |
| Which SPELL_CAST_START rows are a cast bar begun — of a unit, inside the round, and of one cooldown | `packages/analysis/src/utils/castCancels.ts` → `castBarStartsOf` / `packages/analysis/src/utils/castCancels.ts` → `castBarStartsInRound` / `packages/analysis/src/utils/castCancels.ts` → `castBarsOfCooldown` | `ownerCastCancels` (its `hardcasts` count and its pairing); `context/ccUse.ts` (CC USE `cast bar started N×, went off M×`); `context/resourceSnapshot.ts` (the kit's `[UNUSED — started N×, never finished]`) | 2026-10-10, FT-T16 D15 "2c" (user approval on real-match samples). One row = one bar begun, a kicked or stopped bar included; an instant spell writes none. `castBarStartsInRound` keeps the rows from the round's start to its end (a Solo Shuffle round's units keep the lines that follow it — the bound the cooldown ledger puts on its casts). `castBarsOfCooldown`: a bar is cooldown X's when its completed cast would have been a press of X (`isPressOfCooldown` — the same id, the canonical id, a talent's pressable replacement, a same-named variant press), so the kit note and the CC USE entry print one N for one spell (unit test in `ccUse.test.ts`; the gate `checkCcUseStartedCounts` holds the two lines equal). Before this the kit note matched the exact id, and a glyphed Hex (211015 and its siblings, live in `observedSpellIdsGenerated.json`) — another id, the same cooldown, whose casts the ledger does count — never got the note: a widening of that note, adopted on deterministic grounds. On the four D15 sample matches it changes nothing (136 never-spent kit entries, 5 with the note before and after); the corpus count is not captured. CC USE's entries for controls on no cooldown ledger (Cyclone, Polymorph …) group the round's remaining bars by English name; "control" there is `ccSpellIds` asked of the cast id and of its effect auras (`castAndEffectIds`). Not clamped to the round: `ownerCastCancels` reads `castBarStartsOf` — see "Not yet unified". |
| How one of the log owner's cast bars ended: went off, kicked, stopped (and what landed on the owner then), refused by the client, or no end row | `packages/analysis/src/utils/castCancels.ts` → `ownerCastBarOutcomes` | `ownerCastCancels` (its cancels = the `stopped` bars with nothing landing on the owner; its median completed bar); `context/timelineSections/castStopped.ts` (the `[CAST STOPPED]` lines) | 2026-10-10, FT-T16 D15 "2b" (user approval on real-match samples, with a tag of its own). The reading `ownerCastCancels` has had since 2026-09-26, moved into one function when the second reader arrived. A bar's rows are looked for from its start to the next bar's start or `JUKE_LOOKBACK_MS`: a SUCCESS with no interruption row before it → completed; else a SPELL_INTERRUPT of the spell on the owner → kicked; else an interruption row (`CAST_INTERRUPTED_REASONS`) → stopped, with `near` = a control / silence aura or a landed displacement within `CANCEL_CC_NEAR_S` (`forcedStopInstantsMs`); else another SPELL_CAST_FAILED of the spell → refused; else none. Three things a line needs and the cancel ledger did not read: a press refused while the bar was still running is not the bar's end — a "not ready" one (`NOT_READY_REASONS`), and one for a reason the same log shows on a press before a bar's SUCCESS or interruption row ("Another action is in progress" 19 ms after the start, 0068182d round 3; learned from the log's rows, no table of client strings) — marked `earlierFailure`; and a completion logged up to `CAST_QUEUE_TOLERANCE_MS` after the next bar began is a completion (`queued`), never "refused" or "no end". Until 2026-10-11 `ownerCastCancels` skipped the `earlierFailure` and `queued` bars, so that no kick-eaten fact moved when the lines arrived (identical JSON on all 14 recorder rounds of the four D15 sample matches: 339 cast bars, 10 with `earlierFailure`, 0 `queued`) — and a bar stopped after a repeated key press had a `[CAST STOPPED]` line while missing from kick-eaten's cancels. It now counts every bar (user decision; the numbers are on the `ownerCastCancels` row), and the gate `checkKickEatenCancelsCoverCastStopped` holds `yourCancels` at or above the number of `not kicked; no control …` lines. A limit both readers share: nothing ties a SUCCESS row to its bar but the window, so the previous cast's SUCCESS logged at or just after a bar's start (a queued chain) reads as that bar's completion, and a bar stopped right after it gets no line and is no cancel (0 of 339 bars on the four matches had a same-spell SUCCESS within `CAST_QUEUE_TOLERANCE_MS` after their start). The log does not tell stopping a cast by hand from moving, and no reader may say either. |

| The HP% printed on a PRESS line — **the signed exception to the render grid** | `packages/analysis/src/utils/cooldowns.ts` → `hpAtPress` | `matchTimeline.ts`'s `getCDTargetAndVelocityPart` (`[YOU] [CD]` / `[YOU] [CC]` / `[YOU] [PROC]`: `self: N% HP`, `→ X (N% HP)`, `lowest ally N% HP`, with the velocity and the 2 s DPS window on the same instant), `healerCastGapFiller.ts`'s `castTargetHpTag` (`[YOU] [CAST] … (N% HP)`), the `[ENEMY DEF]` `(at N% HP)` / `(target at N% HP)` and `[ENEMY TRINKET]` `(target at N% HP)` renders, and `extractMajorCooldowns`' `cast.targetHpPct` (the `[UNNECESSARY]` threshold and the `questionable-external` fact); the gate `checkSameSecondHpConsistency` skips these lines through the exported `PRESS_HP_LINE_TAGS` | **User ruling 2026-09-30 (triage A21; hp-state F-R8 + enemy-def F-E11).** HP on a press line is the unit's HP AT THE PRESS — its last advanced sample strictly before the press, and before the press's own heal on that unit when that heal is logged in the `PRESS_EFFECT_LEAD_MS` (50) ahead of the cast line — not the `[STATE]` reading of the displayed second. A press made in the closest call of a round read like an ordinary moment on the grid (bd790c92 Bear Form 23 % → 8 %; 64a7a24d Restoral "lowest ally 64 %" was the Restoral heal itself, 40 % before it). Not the nearest sample: an instant heal's healed sample sits a millisecond before its own SUCCESS line (06bb9860 Lay on Hands would read 89 % for 32 %). | How hard a unit was being hit at an instant (damage taken **plus** damage a shield ate)                                | `packages/analysis/src/utils/incomingPressure.ts` → `incomingPressureEvents`           | `cooldowns.ts` → `computePressureWindows` (and through `criticalWindows.ts`, the dense-sampling ranges); `matchTimelineSections.ts`'s `[DMG SPIKE]` absorb annotation; `matchTimeline.ts`'s incoming-DPS velocity string; `resourceSnapshot.ts`'s focus-target pick; `matchArchetype.ts`'s `totalDamageReceived` / `peakDamageInWindow`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | A hit a shield ate whole never reaches `damageIn` — the log reports it as a standalone `SPELL_ABSORBED`, so `damageIn` alone missed **22.2%** of incoming effective HP (600 new-season archive rounds), spec-dependent from 0.9% (Preservation Evoker) to 35.4% (Arcane Mage) — a bias of up to 35pp on any cross-spec pressure comparison. Two failures this closed: `computePressureWindows` was damage-only, and the `[DMG SPIKE]` annotation scanned `damageIn` for `SPELL_ABSORBED` — a shape that array cannot hold — printing on 0 of 2,952 windows. `sumIncomingPressure` / `sumAbsorbedPressure` are window sums over this same list — a consumer must take one of the three, never re-merge the two arrays itself. Amounts are POSITIVE magnitudes, unlike `damageIn`'s negative `effectiveAmount`. A partly absorbed hit is not double-counted: the damage record's `amount` is already net of the absorb, so its `effectiveAmount` (`amount − overkill`, `convert.ts` → `hpLost`) is the health lost and the absorb event is the part the shield ate — together the whole hit. Until 2026-10-01 `convert.ts` subtracted the absorbed part a second time (adjudication #13), under-reading every partly absorbed hit; reversed by user ruling A38. **Redistribution** (triage hp-state F-D1; user ruling 2026-09-30, A22 = B): a row whose spell is in `REDISTRIBUTION_DAMAGE_IDS` (Spirit Link 98021, Void Leech 451963; registered in `curatedIdRegistry`) and whose source is on the unit's own roster side is a teammate's health being moved, not an enemy hitting the unit, and is left out — the damage row and the absorbed part alike. Before, 5e8b11c1's healer "took a 1.10M spike", 685k of it his own Spirit Link Totem, while the `Top sources` of that same line listed 106k / 73k / 58k. Blessing of Sacrifice's transfer 6940 and a charmed teammate's hits stay in (same ruling). Every consumer passes `sides` (`buildRosterSides`); without it the row's own reaction flags decide, which is wrong only while someone is charmed. **2026-10-10 (WP-A1 3, T12 ① c; user ruling: "windows, damage spikes and kill-attempt lines must not run past the target's death or the round's end")**: a victim's `computePressureWindows` buckets close at min(`firstDeathMs(victim)`, `roundEndMs(combat)`) — no hit after the close is summed, no bucket starts after it, and the returned `toSeconds` IS the close; which buckets are kept is still decided on the nominal 10 s span. Cut at the source, so every `pressureWindows` reader gets the same span (`[CC BOOKMARK]`'s `in the [DMG SPIKE] a–b`, `[OFFENSIVE WINDOW]`'s peak-spike interval and marker, the positioning spike windows, the desktop pressure lanes). On the line, `in Ns` is `renderedWindowSeconds` of the displayed endpoints (the DPS and the %/s divide by it) and the end HP is 0 when `isDeadAtRenderSecond` at the end second. Do not re-derive a bucket's end as `from + 10`. 605-file numbers: see the commit. |
| How much damage a unit TOOK in a window — landed hits only, a shield's share left out, a teammate's redistribution left out | `packages/analysis/src/utils/incomingPressure.ts` → `sumLandedPressure` | `dispelAnalysis.ts` (`postCcDamage` of a missed and a late cleanse window: the `Nk taken` of `[UNCLEANSED DEBUFF]`, missed-cleanse `facts.postCcDamageK` and its cap order, and BACKLOG #39's consequence gate `consequenceDemotes`) | Triage missed-cleanse F-C1 (2026-10-06). The sum used to read `damageIn` raw, so a Voidweaver's Void Leech on the CC'd ally counted as damage the missed dispel cost (6062daf2: `18k taken`, all of it two Void Leech rows from the owner; 0e0663e6: 65k of which 37k). It is the non-absorb half of `incomingPressureEvents`, so the redistribution rule is the SAME one (`REDISTRIBUTION_DAMAGE_IDS`, source on the unit's roster side — user ruling A22 = B); every other same-side row stays in (a self-sourced deferral such as Time Dilation is enemy damage paid late). Landed-only on purpose: #39's 22 / 125 zero-consequence baseline was measured on landed damage (on the unfiltered sum), and folding absorbs in is a separate call. A Critical window whose only damage was redistribution now demotes to High — the ruled behaviour for zero damage, not a new rule. |
| Whether an absorb event prevented damage or only DELAYED it (Time Dilation, Stretch Time) — so delayed damage is counted once, when the health is lost | `packages/analysis/src/utils/incomingPressure.ts` → `isDeferralAbsorb` (table: `DEFERRAL_SHIELD_DAMAGE_IDS`, shield id → the id its delayed damage lands as; `isDeferredTickId` for the tick side) | `incomingPressure.ts` (`incomingPressureEvents` and everything that sums it: `[DMG SPIKE]`, the press-line DPS, `computePressureWindows`, cd-hoarded's `dmg2s`; `incomingPressureBySchool`), `context/timelineHelpers.ts` (`↳ Top sources` / `Top damage in final 10s`; `DEFERRED_DAMAGE_SPELL_IDS` is the table's values), `utils/externalDamage.ts` (`(+Ak absorbed, +Dk deferred)` on `[ENEMY DEF] … during it`), `utils/counterfactual.ts` (`computeMitigationAudit`'s `deferred` row) → prompt `formatMitigationAuditLine` and desktop `DeathRecapCard.tsx`; gate `packages/eval/scripts/deferredDamageScan.ts` (DOUBLE must be 0; RECONCILE re-runs the arithmetic) | FT-T02b, user ruling 2026-10-09 (option B: "伤害在真正掉血的时刻计"). The log writes the delayed half of a hit as a SPELL_ABSORBED by the shield and again as the self → self tick that takes the health. On the 60 raw logs of the 2026-10-08 re-eval Time Dilation "absorbed" 21,686,939 and its ticks came back as 19,480,882 landed + 1,764,448 absorbed by a real shield (98.0 %); Stretch Time 8,325,694 vs 7,292,177 + 941,210 (98.9 %) — delayed, not prevented, and both records were being summed. Rule: a deferral shield's SPELL_ABSORBED is not absorbed damage; the tick is the damage (landed, or absorbed when a real shield eats the tick). **One exception, by the nature of the fact**: a per-school reading asks what was thrown at the unit, and the log writes both tick ids as school 0x1 (physical) whatever was delayed — `incomingPressureBySchool` keeps the hit under its own school at the time it was thrown and leaves the tick out. The mitigation audit prints such a shield as `deferred ~Nk … — delayed, not prevented`, the amount read off the log (`absorbContributionsInWindow`), not back-computed. NOT changed: Time Dilation stays 50 % in the mitigation table for kill-window pricing (user decision 2026-07-30). |
| Whether an event's source is on the victim's own team | `packages/analysis/src/utils/rosterSide.ts` → `isSameSideSource` | `timelineHelpers.ts`'s `getTopDamageSourcesInWindow` (the `Top sources` of `[DMG SPIKE]`, `Top damage in final Ns` on death blocks, `killed by:` on `[UNIT DESTROYED]`, the match-end killer line); `incomingPressure.ts`'s redistribution rule (row above) | Triage death-kill F-T1 + hp-state F-D1 (2026-10-01). The side is a ROSTER fact read from the source's GUID — `buildRosterSides`: a unit's `reaction` is the parser's vote over the whole round, and a summon takes its owner's. The per-event reaction flags are not: while a player is charmed the log writes that player on the other side, and while the log's own recorder is charmed it flips everyone. The flag test dropped the enemy's damage as "same team" (ba8c0510: 86k of a 199k Ray of Frost missing from Top sources; 17 of the 60 triage rounds carry flipped rows), and would keep an enemy priest's Void Leech on a charmed teammate out of the pressure total (17 of 2,649 Void Leech rows on the 605-file capture slice). A CHARM is the one thing the roster cannot see: a row that flags its source or its victim as a charmed player (`isControlledPlayerFlags`, PET type on a Player GUID — the recorder too) is an attack across the charm and never same-side, so a Mind-Controlled teammate's hits and a team's hits on its own charmed player stay in Top sources as they stay in the pressure total (ruling A22; 605-file slice, `fix-T1015/mcprobe.ts`: 429 rows / 577k from a charmed source in 107 rounds, 166 rows / 1.13M from teammates on a charmed recorder — the roster alone dropped both). Flags remain the fallback for a GUID the roster lacks and for a unit whose roster vote is Neutral. Not routed through it yet: `damageEventLabel`'s choice of which roster map names a source (it has its own full-name rule), and the two readers under "Not yet unified" (2026-10-02). |
| The dampening % stated at an instant — which rules the round runs under, the logged stacks, and what is stated before the first one (in 2v2: one dose below it, said to be derived) | `packages/analysis/src/utils/dampening.ts` → `dampeningRulesOf` (the one bracket classification: the literal bracket string decides; the roster count is only the fallback for a string that names no bracket, and it counts PLAYERS whatever list it is handed) / `packages/analysis/src/utils/dampening.ts` → `getInitialDampening` (the rule's home: the value before the first logged stack — in 2v2 that stack minus `DAMPENING_DOSE_PCT`, `null` when the round logged none) / `packages/analysis/src/utils/dampening.ts` → `buildDampeningEvents` (the stack events, aura 110310 doses) / `packages/analysis/src/utils/dampening.ts` → `getDampeningPercentage` (the reading at an instant; `null` where none is stated) | the timeline's single `dampeningAt` reading on `allPlayers` (`context/matchTimeline.ts` → ctx): the `DAMPENING (…)` header and `[DAMPENING ALERT: N%]` (`timelineSections/dampening.ts`), the `\| dampening: N%` note on `[YOU] [CD]` / `[PROC]` lines (`ownerCd.ts`) and on both `[DEATH]` families, `[MATCH END] damp:`; `benchmark/metrics.ts` (dampening at death); `utils/enemyCDs.ts` (`computeDampening` → a burst window's `dampeningPct`); `candidates/crisisNoResponse.ts` (the `dampeningPct` fact); desktop `report/derive/dampeningSeries.ts` (`buildDampeningEvents` + `getInitialDampening`: the lane and the scrub readout). Gate `packages/eval/src/quality/promptQualityCheck.ts` → `checkDampeningStartConsistency` — a text predicate; the one thing it imports from the producer is the dose step (`packages/analysis/src/utils/dampening.ts` → `DAMPENING_DOSE_PCT`) | WP-H (FT-T13), 2026-10-10. **D10**: one 2v2 prompt stated two start values (header 30 %, press lines 10 %) because three consumers handed the rule table every unit of the round — pets and totems tipped a 2v2 into the "more than four units = 3v3" fallback. A caller whose event list is one side passes `roster` for the classification. **User ruling 2026-10-10 (D11, "按日志第一跳倒推", confirmed the same day against a real round), re-opening the signed O10 of 2026-09-30: a 2v2 round's start is derived from its first logged stack — one dose below it — and the prompt says it is derived.** The log prints no value before the first stack event, and what it prints first contradicts the hand table (42 / 22 at 0:10–0:14 in all 580 2v2 contexts of the 605-file capture), so the start is 41 / 21 per round, never a table value. Header: `started at N% (derived: one 1% step below the first logged stack, M% at m:ss — the log prints no value before that)` or `n/a — no dampening stack was logged in this round`; before m:ss every `\| dampening:` note, the crisis-no-response fact, the benchmark sample, the 0:00 alerts and the desktop series read N; a round with no logged stack states nothing. (PV368 shipped "no number before the first logged stack" — the implementer's reading, replaced by PV369.) 3v3 and Solo Shuffle keep their flat 10 — also a hand value, but the first stack does not contradict it, and the ruling is about 2v2. Gate: before the first `[DEATH]` no `\| dampening: M%` reads below a `started at N%` header; under a derived header the step is re-done from the rendered numbers (N = M − `DAMPENING_DOSE_PCT`) and every `\| dampening:` / `damp:` value stamped before that second reads N; under the no-stack header no line carries `\| dampening: N%`, `[DAMPENING ALERT: N%]` or `damp: N%`. WP-H 3: the one place a dose's stack count is read (`doseStackCount`) tolerates `"42\r"`, which documents stored before the parser's CRLF fix carry. **Do not hand 2v2 a table value again, do not classify the bracket from a unit count, and do not add a reader that calls the rule table with its own list.** Unit tests only — the after numbers were not measured on a capture; 605-file numbers: see the commits. |

### Talent ownership

| Fact                                                                                            | Authoritative predicate                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Consumed by                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Notes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

| Does THIS player actually have spell X in THIS round                                            | `packages/analysis/src/utils/talentOwnership.ts` → `talentOwnershipOf`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `deathOutcomeAnalysis.ts` (availableImmunities + missedExternals gates — feeds the prompt's DEATHS WITH MISSED OPTIONS, deepDive's immunity/external facts, and the desktop DeathRecapCard through the shared `buildDeathOutcomeSummary`)        | Three-state (`yes`/`no`/`unknown`); only a confirmed `no` may filter — `unknown` is reserved for genuine data absence (old archives, unloaded tables) and must pass through. Sources covered: class/spec/hero trees (choice nodes count only the chosen entry), the official per-spec PvP-talent pool (`pvpTalentPoolGenerated`, incl. the ActionBar carrier), the PvP replacement relation, and baseline-by-elimination (in neither trees nor pool → every player of the spec has it). Cast evidence this round always wins; `talentOwnershipFromTables` is the same verdict WITHOUT cast evidence — audits use it so casts can serve as the independent contradiction check (`packages/desktop/scripts/auditTalentOwnership.ts`). Whitelist source classifications are pinned by `packages/analysis/test/talentWhitelistClassification.test.ts`. Solo Shuffle: talents change between rounds, so always pass the CURRENT round's unit — never cache a verdict across rounds by player name/id. `extractMajorCooldowns` predates this export and keeps its own equivalent internal filter (kit-builder policy differs: it _excludes_ unknown non-tree spells without cast/PvP evidence). |

A talent modifier has none: scan run 1 split holders with the plain predicate and all 302 Barkskin casters "held" the Guardian-only Reinforced Fur, all 236 Holy Divine Protection casters the Retribution-only Shield of Vengeance. This wrapper answers `no` for a talent outside the caster's spec trees and pool, otherwise defers to `talentOwnershipOf`. The scan and the resolver import the same function so a promoted row is validated on exactly the population it is applied to. Pinned by `packages/analysis/test/talentModifierOwnership.test.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Which racial the player demonstrably has, and whether a CC was broken by one                    | `packages/analysis/src/data/racialAbilities.ts` → `RACIAL_ABILITIES`; `packages/analysis/src/data/racialAbilities.ts` → `BREAK_RACIAL_SPELL_IDS`; `packages/analysis/src/data/racialAbilities.ts` → `OFFENSIVE_RACIAL_SPELL_IDS`; `packages/analysis/src/data/racialAbilities.ts` → `SHARED_CD_RACIAL_SPELL_IDS`; `packages/analysis/src/data/racialAbilities.ts` → `TRINKET_RACIAL_SHARED_LOCKOUT_MS` | `ccTrinketAnalysis.ts` (binds a break racial to the CC it removed → `trinketState: "racial_break"`, keeping it out of `missedTrinketWindows`); `cooldowns.ts` `extractMajorCooldowns` (offensive racials enter the ledger on cast evidence only) | The combat log carries NO race field, so ownership is **passive only**: an observed cast proves possession, absence proves nothing — unlike `talentOwnershipOf`, this predicate may never yield a "no". The set = the break racials + the class abilities with a DB2 mechanic-immunity aura that the corpus shows ending a hard CC (Blink, Berserker Shout / Rage, Lichborne, Icebound Fortitude; tier-C scan `c19_e21.py`, 605 files) + the racials logged only as a buff (`AURA_KEYED_BREAK_RACIALS`: Stoneform 65116, Fireblood 273104 — their cast ids have 0 SPELL_CAST_SUCCESS, so they were dead as cast-keyed). Owner alive / reaction-ready / not CC'd / not in a casting lockout (aura 60 / 263); target alive / not in a CC / no mechanic-blocking aura (unknown mask → blocked); single-target reach `ccThreatReachYards` (cast range, else caster-centred radius — not the range + radius of externals); LoS not falsified; DR not Immune; no known ready self-breaker (`kitSpellReadyAt`). The 978 landings that moved prime → gated converted at 3.4 % — under what stays prime, over what was gated; prime still converts 2.4× gated (2.7× before), 3.3 points apart both ways. Under the gate, PROMPT_VERSION 377 capture: 3,450 failures in 1,088 of 3,520 owner contexts (28,237 kill-attempt lines) — `softer target then: X — PRIME` 1,915 (652 distinct), the target printed PRIME 1,160 (407), a gated list leaving an `[UNUSED]` wall out 375. **Can add and remove candidate rows**: burst-into-mitigation fires on "the focused target is not prime while another enemy is" — a prime alternative that becomes gated removes a row, a prime focused target that becomes gated adds one. Stale, not regenerated: `ATTEMPT_INTO_TRINKET_OUTCOME_REF` (`signalOutcomeProbe.ts` reads `opportunity.tier` and the prime alternative). The `defenseless` kill-window span still reads the unit's casts only — see "Not yet unified". |

Before, each end and every mid-span second read whoever stood nearest at that instant, so "A→B yd" paired two enemies (605 capture: 974 of 2,156 STAYED IN lines, 582 of 1,121 KITED lines; s0/1-6-16 read "stayed in 3→1.2" while the start enemy went out to 21.9 yd). Returns null — the old rule, for the WHOLE span, never mixed — when no enemy damage landed, two enemies tie for the most, or that enemy has no distance at the span's first or last second. The entry gate reads the measured enemy, so a span whose top damager starts beyond 12 yd yields no line and no candidate (accepted by the user on the preview: position-mistake 341 rows → +8 / −150 on the 605 capture, all `stayed-in`). The STAYED IN line's `(nearest enemy A–B yd over the window)` and position-mistake's `minDist` / `maxDist` stay the nearest of ANY enemy — the two section headers (`STAYED_IN_SECTION_HEADER`, `KITED_SECTION_HEADER`) and the position-mistake legend say which is which. A KITED line prints no span end, so the gate cannot re-derive its measured enemy (see "Not yet unified"). Pinned by `t12MeasuredEnemy.test.ts` (analysis) and the G4d block of `positioningScan.test.ts` (gate; a producer → gate round trip included). |
| Whether a STAYED IN / KITED sample at a rendered second would be taken on the log owner's corpse (the owner already dead at that second's first instant) | `packages/analysis/src/utils/positionAnalysis.ts` → `burstSpanSampledAfterDeath` (`isDeadAt` — the file's dead-at predicate, the one `nearestEnemyAt` asks of every enemy — at `renderS.000`) | `positionAnalysis.ts` (`computeOwnerPositionEvents`, asked of a burst span's LAST rendered second: true ⇒ no STAYED_IN / KITED event, so no POSITIONING line, no position-mistake `stayed-in` row, no deep-dive item and no desktop key moment); gate `positioningScan.ts` G4e (`G4_OWNER_DEAD`: asked of every second a STAYED IN / KITED line prints a distance at — the start, a STAYED line's end, a KITED line's peak) | 2026-10-11. `getUnitPositionAtTime` holds a unit's last position for the 1.5 s interpolation guard, and a dead player's last sample is the death: a span whose last rendered second fell inside that 1.5 s was measured to the spot the owner died on, and a span that began inside it was built from nothing else (605-file capture of f8ce87ae, 3,520 prompts, the owner dead in 702: 16 STAYED IN lines end after the owner's death second and 1 starts after it — 15 of the 17 are also position-mistake `stayed-in` rows, every one with `hpMin=0` — and 2 KITED peaks sit after it; all within 2 s of the death). The span is DROPPED, not cut at the death: a death further than 1.5 s inside a span already gave no event (no end position), and cutting would make the owner's last seconds assessable and add stays (T12 ① b: +53 `stayed-in` rows when the window object was clamped). The instant, not `isDeadAtRenderSecond`: a span whose last rendered second IS the death second samples it before the death and stays (8 STAYED IN lines) — the `[STATE]` tick of that second reads `dead`. A dropped stay frees its `POSITION_MISTAKE_CAP` slot, so a stay that was over the cap can enter the menu. Not covered: a KITED line prints no span end, so the gate cannot see a span the producer should have dropped whose peak precedes the death; MISSED_PUSH still reads the held position (a run can extend through the 1.5 s after the owner's death). |

Corpus, 605 files, the victim's first cast of a locked school as a fraction of the kick's own lockout, 15 holder pairs: 8 dated before the cutover at ×0.344–×0.456 (seven within 12 ms of 0.35 × the lockout, all 289 ms or more before 0.6 × it); 7 since, six at ×0.622–×1.225 and one at ×0.351. A first cast more than 15 ms before the modelled end: 9 of 15 with ×0.6 alone → 1 of 15 dated. The date is the SPELL_INTERRUPT row's own timestamp, a required argument (a reader that does not pass it does not compile); a timestamp that is not a number takes the current ×0.6. A shorter lock exempts less, so this can ADD candidate rows on a pre-hotfix holder's log. Not measured: logs before 12.1, an Elemental holder before the hotfix, Chain Lightning. Pinned by `packages/analysis/test/triageG12CannotCast.test.ts`. |

Why: nothing applied a talent layer, so buffs the game runs longer were priced at `cast + base`, and because the pairing tolerance is ±2 s the REAL `SPELL_AURA_REMOVED` was rejected as belonging to another cast. An entry needs THREE things, not two: the DB2 modifier row (aura 107/108 with `EffectMiscValue_0` = 1 = SPELLMOD_DURATION) **whose `SpellClassOptions` mask actually covers the spell**, a corpus caster split, and arithmetic that reconciles against the table's own base. Since triage position F-S4 (user ruling 2026-09-30, A60 = B) the STAYED IN line's tag selects on it too: `(near-death — the stay was costly)` when true, the fact `(HP stayed at or above 35%)` otherwise — the old `<=` test tagged hpMin = 35 near-death while the menu gate did not count it. 2026-10-10 (WP-E 6, FT-T03, ruling D7): the decision still reads `ownerHpMinPct` (the whole-second minimum) — which stays are candidates, their order, the cap, the desktop key moment, deepDive's item. The PRINTED number (`(min over window)`, `facts.hpMin`) is `ownerHpLowPct`, the trough. Where the two readings sit on different sides of the line the STAYED IN line prints NEITHER tag: `(HP stayed at or above 35%)` would be false of the printed number, and `(near-death — …)` would be a verdict the menu gate did not give. The gate: B not above A; A equals the `[STATE]` tick of the span's first displayed second when that tick carries the log owner; no `[STATE]` tick of the log owner on a whole second inside the span — the first displayed second included — below B; `stayed at or above N%` needs N = the constant and B ≥ N; `near-death` needs B < N. **2026-10-11: the three HP numbers are read on the window the line prints** (`fmtTime(from)–fmtTime(to)`, the rendered seconds the distances are sampled on): `ownerHpStartPct` = `gridHpPct` at the rendered start second, `ownerHpMinPct` = `gridHpMinInWindow` over those seconds, the trough = `hpTroughInWindow` with those seconds as its ticks and the burst span's own milliseconds as its `span`. Before, the start was the raw sampler at the window's fractional start, the minimum a hand-rolled loop of raw readings from `ceil(from)` (no clamp at 100, no stop at the death, seeded with the off-grid start) and the trough's first tick `ceil(from)` — the tick of the second the line begins on was in none of them, and the gate skipped that second. Text check on the 605-file capture of dd91ca98 (1,153 STAYED IN lines with an HP clause, 717 of them with an owner tick on their start second): the printed start differs from that tick on 508, and the tick is below the printed minimum on 24; the tightened gate fails 532 times in 417 owner views there. After: the capture of this commit (not taken here). The DECISION reading moves with it, so `position-mistake` candidates can appear and disappear (authorised by the user): a stay whose only reading under the line was the off-grid start, or the raw reading of the owner's death second, leaves; one whose start-second tick is under the line enters. The death-second case is OPEN — see "Not yet unified". |

The cap itself is the signed 2026-08-23 ruling and is NOT changed; until now nothing in the prompt said the list was capped. The count is the candidates the cap dropped — the same walk carried on, never a second derivation — so no candidate can move; a window starting past the match end is not counted (it would not have printed without the cap either). The count is not re-derivable from text (the dropped windows are what the prompt does not print); it is pinned on the selection by unit tests. The count line opens on a word, not on a timestamp or a number, so the existing `[DMG SPIKE]` gates (anchored on the `m:ss–m:ss` prefix) do not see it — keep it that way. The cap is team-wide, not per target (two comments that said otherwise were corrected). **Do not derive the dropped windows by a second selection, and do not give another reader `notListed`: it exists for the legend.** Unit tests only; 605-file numbers: see the commit. |

Cut at the source, so every reader moves together: `[VULNERABLE]`, `[KILL WINDOW] … (defenseless a–b)`, the healer view, kick-priority(-missed / -team)'s `windowTo` fact and its admission (the candidates that pointed at a target already dead are gone), missed-purge's kill-window priority, the burst ledger's targeting audit, the desktop vuln cards. Unit tests only; 605-file numbers: see the commits. **2026-10-10 (FT-T12 D3):** WHICH control may be credited is no longer a credit-line matter and is not decided in this module: the engine keeps a control in `responseCasts` only when its target was hitting the pressured unit (`controlTargetHitPressured`, its own row), so `creditedAnswer` and the control clause can name only such targets, and `responded` reads the same list — unlike the two marks above, this rule DOES reach `responded` (605 preview: 0 slow-defensive-response candidates added or removed). Exclusions (codex R1/R2): blocked anywhere in the window, channel in flight, > 40 yd, LoS false OR unknown, mana < 10 %, and — user ruling 2026-09-19 「如果已经有人死了 就不要提示」 — any player on either side already dead at the crossing (`priorDeath`, evaluated last; `priorDeathSide` keeps the side in the scan rows). That last one removed 56 of the 57 clean-idle points of the 1/10 archive slice: the card had been describing a healer who stopped playing a 2v3. Clean idle additionally needs no cast, no cast start, both endpoint positions known and < 8 yd apart, not inside a 15 s no-cast stretch (DC / AFK class), teammate did not answer either. The answered comparator enters the table only after the SAME exclusions. `diedWithin10s` is table-only.                                                                    |

Five Solo Shuffle logs, 30 rounds (`fix-FT/scripts/upr_windowEnds.ts`): of the 59 windows that ran past the round's end, 41 ended on a removal logged after `combat.endTime` (up to 6.0 s after the death), 10 on one between the death and `combat.endTime`, 8 had no removal row and ran to `combat.endTime` — Power Infusion up 7.7 s when the round ended at 2:29 read `unpurged for 14s`. Cut at the source, so no reader holds a second length. It moves rows, by mechanism: a buff up for under 3 s inside the round, or applied after the ending death, has no window; purgers free only after the round's end are locked out; and a purge of ours logged after the round's end no longer answers the window — the uncleansed windows' rule (`!clippedAtRoundEnd`). No threshold, priority, cap or feasibility rule changed. The gate takes the grid and nothing more: the line's second S is the application floored, N the length rounded, so a cut window has S + N ≤ R + 1 (R the round-end second); an overrun of 2.5 s or more always fails, a shorter one can sit inside the grid's second. | The rendered line format of a baseline review card's candidate evidence (`<type> <units> {k=v, …}`) | `packages/eval/src/explore/baselineFindings.ts` → `candidateEvidence` | `baselineToCards` (renders the line); `packages/eval/src/explore/baselineFindings.ts` → `parseCandidateEvidenceLine`, through which `answersAlignment.ts` recovers the candidate type behind a human-reviewed card (GH #18) | Renderer and parser deliberately live side by side in one file so the format has exactly one home; their inverse relation is pinned by the round-trip test in `explore.answersAlignment.test.ts`. Registered 2026-08-21 when `answersAlignment.ts` became `answers.json`'s second consumer. Never re-derive the line parse at a call site. |
| **Observed** candidate-menu incidence per type for one sample and one owner mode — the cross-check on the registry's declared status (presence proves a type fires; absence proves nothing) | `packages/eval/scripts/candidateDiagnostics.ts` → `scanCandidateIncidence` | `npx tsx packages/eval/scripts/candidateDiagnostics.ts --n 400 --json`; its `rows[].type` set is the generation universe of the coach-corpus negative control (`tools/coach-corpus/negative_control.py --universe`, GH #74); the headers of `packages/analysis/src/data/candidateTypeFlags.ts` and the desktop's `derive/mistakes.ts` → `IGNORED_CANDIDATE_TYPES` both point here | GH #76 (2026-09-12). Not a liveness oracle: it only calls `extractCandidateFindings`, so the two desktop-derived rows (missed-kick / missed-purge-kill-window) are invisible to it, and absence in one owner mode is not non-liveness — burst-into-mitigation was 0 under `--owner logger` and 90 under `--owner dps` with no product change (GH #75); `--owner all` is the widest control. A type can be dead **five** ways and no single place lists them: `CANDIDATE_TYPE_FLAGS` false · emitter kept but no longer called from the assembly (mana-\*) · emitter deleted (cc-locked, wasted-trinket, death-unused-defensive, juked-kick, dr-clipped-cc, burst-into-immunity, off-target-in-window, unconverted-burst) · `BRACKET_TYPE_ALLOWLIST` · the desktop `IGNORED_CANDIDATE_TYPES` set, which also mixes retired with menu-only-by-design (kick-eaten, md-cyclone-window, death\*, missed-cleanse). Four types are double-killed, so flipping one switch back silently does nothing. Four independent code-reading counts of the live set came out 49 → 47 → 37 → 31; the scan (16 types on 400 rounds, 2026-09-06) was the only correct one. Since 2026-09-12 the five places derive from one table, `data/candidateTypeRegistry.ts` → `CANDIDATE_TYPE_REGISTRY` (row above); this scan remains the observational check that what the table calls live actually fires. |

Two consumers inside one screen, not an analysis/gate pair — see **Scope** above.

## Feature flag state

Flag values are **configuration, not code location**, so they do not belong in
the index table's prose — that is exactly how six statements in this repo came
to assert the opposite of the running code after the 2026-08-15 flip. They live
here instead, in a machine-parsed table: `predicateIndex.test.ts` reads the
rows **by column** and asserts each flag's runtime value equals `Expected`.
Flip a flag without updating this table and CI goes red.

Deliberately column-parsed rather than matched against English prose: synonyms
("disabled by", "initially false") slip through, the Chinese companion doc
("默认关") cannot match an English pattern at all, and — worst — a prose matcher
silently stops matching when the wording changes, which is precisely when it
needs to fire.

## Not yet unified

**Recorded 2026-10-11, CLOSED the same day (codex post-hoc review 45-FT-101 of the dated Storm Conduit numbers and of Lethal Calibration)** — two readings that could make a cooldown or a cast read available when the game would not have allowed it. (1) `logDatedNumberAt` (`packages/analysis/src/utils/logEra.ts`) gave the OLD value to any timestamp before the cutover, but the parser dates a line without a signed UTC offset in the parsing machine's zone, so a post-hotfix match recorded east of UTC and imported further east is dated up to 14 h early — 4 s a cast and a ×0.35 lockout for a log that should read 2 s and ×0.6. The old value is now taken only for a timestamp at least `LOG_ZONE_UNCERTAINTY_MS` (14 h) before the cutover, i.e. before it in every zone; inside that window and for a non-date it is the current value, the less accusing side for both halves. Cost: a real pre-hotfix log from the last 14 h before 2026-08-18 00:00 UTC reads the current numbers. (2) `eventTriggerTimesMs` (`packages/analysis/src/data/talentScriptedCooldowns.ts`) counted every Wildfire Bomb damage / ABSORB row as an enemy hit; one use now credits each destination unit once. Still open: whether a pet, guardian or totem the bomb hits counts as "an enemy" for Lethal Calibration (the reader counts any destination unit; the corpus fit that adopted 2 s per hit can only falsify a model that is too long, not one that credits too much) — Boomstick is response-only, so no candidate row reads it.

**Recorded 2026-10-11, OPEN (X1; counted on the 605 capture's text, the DB2 rows read at 12.1.0.69587)** — Blessing of Protection / Blessing of Spellwarding: one cooldown in the menu, still two elsewhere. (1) *The kit.* The loadout lists the two side by side, each with its own seconds and its own `[UNUSED]` — `Blessing of Protection [300s, lasts 10s], Blessing of Spellwarding [180s, lasts 6s]`: 887 kit lines in 828 contexts (125 the log owner's, 238 a teammate's, 524 an enemy's). Left as it is: the kit has no vocabulary for one cooldown with two buttons. (2) *Which number.* The 180 s is a hand value (`SPELL_EFFECT_OVERRIDES`, `data/spellEffectOverrides.ts`). DB2 gives neither blessing a recovery of its own (SpellCooldowns rows 132 and 23471 hold the global cooldown only) and the shared pool 300 s (SpellCategory 1392). **Recorded 2026-10-11, OPEN (the dated rules are asked with the parser's date of a log, not the instant its lines state)** — a log recorded EAST of UTC writes its UTC offset without a sign (`8/18/2026 18:56:32.16710` is .167 and +10; 7,082 of the 18,134 new-season files, 225 of the 605-file sample), and `parseTimestamp` (`packages/parser/src/l1/timestamp.ts`) reads those digits as more fraction and the wall clock in the zone of the machine doing the parsing. On the machine that recorded the log that is the same instant; on any other it is off by the gap between the two zones — an Oceanic log parsed on a US Eastern machine is dated 14 hours late. Every reader of an absolute epoch was classified. (a) **Two epochs of one parse subtracted** — every in-match time, durations, DR / cooldown arithmetic, the Solo Shuffle round stitching: unaffected. (b) **A parsed epoch against the machine's own clock** — the recording join (`packages/desktop/src/main/recordingsStore.ts` `associate`, 60 s tolerance; `recorder.ts`'s match-open split), the library's order and "played at", the date filter and day grouping of the match list: for a user's own logs the machine-zone reading is the RIGHT one, exactly, and it is why the parser's reading must not move — a half-hour zone is written as a whole hour (the 164 Australia/Adelaide files say `9`), so the stated instant of such a user's own match is 30 min late and would miss its recording. (c) **A raw.txt line re-read against a stored document's epoch** (`parseRawStreams`' `baseMs`; the stored document has no raw lines): the two must be the same function, so a changed reading shifts the raw streams of every stored east-of-UTC match that was parsed in another zone — and the same breaks today when a library is moved between zones. (d) **A parsed epoch against a calendar constant** — `logIsFrom`'s readers (`drResetMsAt`, the Stellar Protection gate, `eventReductionSecondsAt`, `kickLockoutVictimMultiplierAt`) and the eval scans' `meta.startTime < PATCH_121_GOLIVE_EPOCH_MS` season filters: the one class that is wrong for another player's log. Match ids are content hashes of the raw lines and depend on none of this. What exists now: `rawLineInstantMs` (the row above) reads the stated instant, and `kickLockoutScan.ts` prints it for every pair it dates. What does not: the dated rules are asked with event timestamps at some two dozen call sites, most of which hold a unit and no match (their own callers are as many again), and the parsed document does not carry the stated start — adding it (an optional field, as `teamMmr` was) has no reader until those chains carry it. Measured on the 605 files as a US Eastern machine parses them: 0 files are on a different side of 12.1 go-live (the sample starts 2026-08-13); 2 are on a different side of the Storm Conduit cutover (61fc7e40, +2, and c67114fb, +9 — both played on the evening of 08-17 local time and dated 08-18 by the parser); neither has a Storm Conduit holder, so no prompt line differs; of the scan's 68 dated pairs, 0. Options, none taken: carry `statedStartTime?` on the parsed match and thread `statedStartTime − startTime` to the four rules; or have the corpus tools hand the parser each file's own stated zone (its `timezone` option) — which is the changed reading of (b) and (c), for those tools only.

**Recorded 2026-10-01, OPEN (triage missed-cleanse F-C8 / F-C9, codex review)** — which position a line-of-sight test reads. `losAnalysis.ts` documents the contract: LoS is topological, so it reads the nearest RAW sample (`getUnitRawPositionAtTime`), and only continuous quantities (distance) may interpolate. `momentSnapshot.ts` follows it, and since F-C9 so does the dispel reach sweep `anyDispellerReachable` (missed-cleanse / missed-purge reach) — its LoS test was never active before F-C9 (the zone sat only under `startInfo`), so it was switched on with raw samples; distance still interpolates. They agree with each other and with the gate (that agreement is their shared predicate today), but an interpolated point between two in-LoS samples can sit inside a pillar and read "not reachable" (codex's case: zone 1505, target samples 4 s apart either side of the north pillar — pinned for the dispel sweep in `packages/analysis/test/dispelReachGrid.test.ts`). Unifying means moving those consumers AND the gate to raw samples in one batch, with a 605-file add / remove count per candidate type (position-mistake, [ROOT], healer exposure, burst-window windows).

**Recorded 2026-10-01, deliberately different (triage kick-eaten F-K6b × kick-priority F-P3, CROSS-THEME §1c)** — how far a melee kicker can reach. kick-eaten's out-range gate reads `gapCloserStateAt` (`utils/gapClosers.ts`): a registered list of charges / leaps / teleports, a 1 s "just used" window, exact-instant charge readiness — and the advice is refused unless the kicker provably had none. kick-priority's accusation reads `meleeKickReachYd` (`analysis/candidates/kickPriority.ts`): a running model of how far the OWNER could close. They are conservative in opposite directions on purpose — out-range advice must assume the kicker CAN close; a "you could have kicked" accusation must be sure the owner could — so one number for both would make one of them wrong. `packages/eval/test/predicateIndex.test.ts` pins both symbols. **Rewritten 2026-10-07 (B-tier X3, user ruling 2026-10-06)**: the two still answer different questions and still err in opposite directions, but they now share ONE number — the run speed `KICK_RUN_SPEED_YD_S` (7 yd/s, `kickPriority.ts`). kick-eaten's `outRangeFact` gained a last condition: `yes` only when the kicker stood farther beyond its kick range than it could walk during the cast (`castWindowS` × `KICK_RUN_SPEED_YD_S`; `castWindowS` = the cast's nominal length or the time it had run at the kick, whichever is longer, from `ccTrinketAnalysis.ts`). So the gap-closer list answers "could it jump in" and the run speed answers "could it walk in"; kick-priority keeps its own envelope (`meleeKickReachYd`: base 8 yd + the same speed, capped at 20 yd) for what the OWNER could close. What stays deliberately un-unified is the envelope around the speed, not the speed.

**Recorded 2026-10-01, OPEN (triage kick-eaten F-K5d × res-readiness F-C5b)** — "is this enemy's kick usable now". kick-eaten's kicker loop asks `castBlockingAuraAt` (the aura half of the cannot-cast predicate). `enemyInterrupts.ts` → `computeEnemyInterruptAvailability` (`enemy interrupts UP`, `[CONTESTED]`) still lists a kicker who is stunned; res-readiness F-C5b (ruling A′16, group G4) is the entry that makes it import the same helper.

**Recorded 2026-10-01, OPEN (triage kick-eaten F-K7b / F-K7a)** — what a kick lockout stops. The post-kick classifier and the kick-eaten text ask it per spell (`schoolLockedBy`: only a spell whose every school is locked), and the text's lock also ends early at `lockEndedBySuccessS`. `buildCannotCastIntervals` (`cannotCastIntervals.ts`) still carries a lockout as one interval for its whole modelled length with no school on it, so its readers (cd-hoarded's owner gate, the kick run budget, `ccInWindowS`, `[RES]` `cc:[kick]`, CONSEQ) cannot tell a Nature-locked healer's Holy button from a Nature one. Narrowing it needs the spell each reader is asking about; kick-eaten F-K5d / F-K6d take only the aura half (`castBlockingAuraIntervals`) for that reason. Storm Conduit's shorter lockout (F-K8, G12) changes the same interval's length. **2026-10-10 (FT-T10, user ruling option B): narrowed for every reader that names a spell.** The lockout interval carries the locked schools (`lockedSchoolMask`); `intervalBlocksSpell` asks it per spell, `cannotCastIntervalsForSpells` / `intervalBlocksEverySpell` per set of spells. First cd-hoarded's owner gate and the sync-window ready gate; then, each previewed on the 605 capture and adopted by the user the same day (cc-avoidable +1 candidate, the others context lines only): missed-purge / missed-steal "purger locked" and missed-cleanse "every dispeller locked" (`dispelAnalysis.ts`), the kick run budget (`kickPriority.ts`), cc-avoidable (`candidateFindings.ts`), `[CD PRIOR]`'s opportunity set (`cdTriggerPrior.ts`), burst-window feasibility (`burstWindowDecisionPoints.ts`), the death block's missed-option tags (`deathOutcomeAnalysis.ts`) and `[DEFENSIVE AVAILABLE]`'s free-before-death (`timelineHelpers.ts`) — the index row "Whether one cannot-cast interval stops a GIVEN spell" lists them. No single spell to ask about, so unchanged by design: healing-gap / HEALER OFFENSE free seconds, death-setup `healer-locked` and its lock-chain facts, the kill sequence's `[HEALER CC]` lock chain, `ccInWindowS`, `[RES]` `cc:[kick]`, CONSEQ, the position / summon-reach "free to act" reads. **(a) CLOSED 2026-10-11** — a pet's purge or kick was asked against its OWNER's intervals; the lockout half went first (review 40-FT-54), and since 2026-10-11 a spell the log shows the unit's pet casting is asked of the pet's own cast-blocking auras and lockouts by every reader that names a spell (`cannotCastIntervalsForSpells` with the round's units; the index row has the corpus numbers and what is still not known about the pet). **Still OPEN**: (b) the kill sequence's `[DEFENSIVE AVAILABLE] … (free Ns before the death)` is per spell while death-setup's `freeBeforeDeathS` reads the unasked intervals — `freeMsBefore`'s comment ties the two numbers together, and they can now differ for one unit; (c) found while verifying this list against the code: `ccSamplerFor` (`ccTargetState.ts`, behind PEEL OPTIONS and CC USE) samples for one known CC and still answers `owner-cc` on any lockout — and on the owner's intervals for a control its pet casts (Seduction, Axe Toss) — it was not one of the previewed readers and needs its own 605 preview before it moves.

**Recorded 2026-10-01, deliberate (triage enemy-def F-E21, user ruling P-b7)** — "is this enemy's PvP trinket ready" for the kill-opportunity tier. `packages/analysis/src/utils/killWindowTargetSelection.ts` → `getTrinketStateAtTime` reads the shared `pvpTrinketUses` (G7-P2) and **deliberately not the racial lock** that `pvpTrinketRemainingSecondsAt` reads from `breakAbilityPresses`: a racial press must not turn a target into the trinket-less PRIME tier (user ruling P-b7, 2026-10-01; the racial × trinket "softer target" question is a separate study). Do not "unify" the two on this point.

**Recorded 2026-10-02 (triage enemy-def F-E21, Fable review)** — what a non-trinket break may be bound to, and the reverse lock. (1) `breakRemovesCc(break, cc)`: the CC's mechanic (`spellMechanics.ts`'s `ccMechanicOf`) must be on the break's own DB2 mechanic-immunity aura (`explicitlyBreaksMechanic`); unknown is no. The 10 ms timing test (`castEndedCcWindow`) alone cannot tell "Blink ended the stun" from "the fear ran out and a queued Blink fired 4 ms later". On 101 of the 605 S2 files (`fix-KA/breakMechProbe.ts`): 235 bound presses before, 233 after — the two it removes are Blink out of Axe Toss 89766, a stun whose DB2 category mechanic is 26 (interrupt). **Known and open**: that mis-keyed mechanic; and Stoneform / Fireblood, which remove by dispel type (not in this data) and so never name the CC they ended — their presses still render and still lock the trinket (0 of the 235 bound presses were theirs). (2) The trinket → racial lock: a CC landing less than `TRINKET_RACIAL_SHARED_LOCKOUT_MS` after a PvP-trinket press prints the player's trinket-equivalent racial as `X: ON CD (Ns left)` (ruling A′15: "and vice versa"). The racial is the one the player is seen pressing this round; the 30 s floor is the constant's own evidence (117 trinket → racial presses, minimum gap 30.1 s). It is a fact note on a friendly CC line only — `getTrinketStateAtTime` still reads neither direction of the lock (P-b7, the paragraph above).

**Recorded 2026-10-01, OPEN (triage enemy-def F-E12)** — a re-announced aura as one press. `packages/analysis/src/utils/enemyDefensives.ts` → `joinReappliedIntervals` joins two back-to-back intervals of one spell from one source unless the source logged a second cast (f4eb8c87: one Divine Shield printed `0.9s` + `7.1s`). It is applied only to the `[ENEMY DEF]` events. Every other reader of `buildAuraIntervals` (the death-window mitigation audit, [STACKED DEFENSIVES], burst-into-mitigation, cooldown ledgers, CC windows) still sees the split, softened only by the builder's own rebroadcast rule (no cast within 1 s of the second APPLIED — which the cast that opened the first interval defeats when the re-announce comes inside that second). Moving the join into the builder changes every one of those readers and needs its own capture.

**Recorded 2026-10-01, OPEN (triage enemy-def F-E5)** — a Feign Death without Survival Tactics. Both readers of "a Feign Death happened" (the cooldown ledger and, since ruling D8 of 2026-10-10, `effectSaves` through `FEIGN_DEATH_ABSORB_AURA_IDS` — until then `IMMUNITY_SAVE_AURA_NAMES`, which no longer holds Feign Death) key on aura 202748, the only logged trace besides `UNIT_DIED … unconscious=1`. The parser keeps that event (`unconsciousEvents`), but `parser-compat` does not carry it onto the analysis units, so a hunter without the PvP talent feigns invisibly (538 of 20,704 feigns in the every-6 archive, A9-EVIDENCE §3). Closing it is a parser-compat change (the G6 line).

**Recorded 2026-10-02, OPEN (triage enemy-def F-E15, Fable review)** — which control a break is credited with, two gaps. (1) `packages/analysis/src/utils/ccTrinketAnalysis.ts` → `bindBreakToWindow` ranks the CCs active at a press by tier and official time left, but its windows do not carry HOW each CC ended: a CC broken by damage (`SPELL_AURA_BROKEN` / `_SPELL`) in the same instant as the press is "ended at the cast" like the one the press removed, and wins the label when it had more official time left. Rare — the trinket's own removal is a `SPELL_AURA_REMOVED`, and of 219 damage breaks near a Medallion cast in the 605-file scan 91 % fall more than 25 ms before it — but the fix needs the removal event on the window. (2) "How long was this CC going to run" has two computations: the binder's `expectedDurationSeconds` (`ccFullDurationForCaster` over enemies + pets × `drDurationFactor` of the caster-keyed, rebroadcast-dropped DR chain) and `packages/analysis/src/utils/ccBreakAnalysis.ts` → `analyzeCcBreaks`'s remaining time (players only, × `OPPRESSING_ROAR_PVP_CC_DURATION_MULT`, DR from `buildCcCategoryHistory`). They share `drDurationFactor` and nothing else, so a roar-lengthened CC or a same-ms rebroadcast can give the `[CC BROKEN]` "had Ns left" and the break binding different lengths for one application. One `expectedCcDurationS(spell, caster, drLevel, roarAtApply)` would close it. **2026-10-10 (WP-G), gap (2) narrowed, not closed**: both computations now take the application's full length from `ccFullDurationForApplication` (the Roar included, and only where it covers the CC's mechanic), so a roar-lengthened CC no longer gives the two different lengths. Still separate: who the caster is looked up among (enemies + pets vs players only) and which DR chain the factor comes from.

**Recorded 2026-10-01, OPEN (triage fix session G6)** — when a channel started and ended. Two readers landed the same day: `packages/analysis/src/utils/castCommitSpans.ts`'s `channelSpans` (missed-cleanse `ownerCastingS`, triage F-C10: a `CHANNELED_SPELL_IDS` success paired with the caster's same-id aura starting within [−`CHANNEL_AURA_LEAD_MS`, +`CHANNEL_AURA_LAG_MS`] = [−1, +100] ms, ending at its REMOVED / BROKEN) and `healerCastGapFiller.ts`'s `channelCutByCc` (`[channel cut by CC after Ns]`, triage other F-O14: the same table and aura, paired within ±250 ms, ending at the first REMOVED). Both go through `dropAuraRebroadcasts`. They differ only in the pairing tolerance and can disagree on a channel whose aura is logged 100–250 ms from its success. `channelCutByCc` should read the span from `channelSpans`; not done here because F-O14 belongs to another fix session and its numbers were measured with ±250 ms. Also open: a channel span has no length cap (a bar and an empower hold are capped at 12 s) — the longest on the 605-file manifest is a 24.8 s Soothing Mist, a real refreshed channel, but an aura left dangling would count as occupied until its REMOVED.

**Recorded 2026-10-01, OPEN (triage fix session G6, found while landing other F-O6)** — which `SPELL_EMPOWER_END` closes an empowered press. `matchTimeline.ts`'s `ownerEmpowerTag` still looks for an END within ±1.5 s of the press, on the stated assumption that the END and the cast's `SPELL_CAST_SUCCESS` are the same instant. They are not: the success is logged at `SPELL_EMPOWER_START`, the END at the release, so a full charge is out of reach. On the 60 triage picks the owner released 56 empowers (52 at level 1, holds 0.35–0.96 s; 4 at level 3, holds 1.74–3.04 s) and **all 4 level-3 releases render without `[EMPOWER L3]`** — 36 tags rendered, every one `L1` (`fix-G6/probes/empower_holds.py`). `packages/analysis/src/utils/castCommitSpans.ts`'s `empowerSpans` pairs START → END exactly and already carries the level; the tag's END lookup (and `castParam.ts`'s 400 ms window, which keys on the aura instead) should read it. Left as is here because it adds rendered tags outside the entries this session was given — a user call.

**Recorded 2026-09-30, OPEN (triage F-H20, user ruling)** — which schools a save covers. cd-hoarded's `coversCrisisSchool` reads `saveSchoolMask` (the signed `MITIGATION_TABLE` mask, else the DB2 absorb mask), so Anti-Magic Shell counts only for a crisis at least `SCHOOL_SAVE_MIN_SHARE` magic. Readers that still see only `MITIGATION_TABLE` and so know nothing about AMS's schools: enemy-def (F-E7) and crisis-external (F-A7) routing — theirs to switch to `saveSchoolMask`. The same ruling puts the 50 % partial-immunity rule (A30, enemy-def F-E24) on the same threshold; when it lands it should import `SCHOOL_SAVE_MIN_SHARE` / `schoolShareCoveredBy`, not a second 0.5. **That leg closed 2026-10-01** (enemy-def F-E7 / F-E24, crisis-external F-A7): `attributeFailure` reads `limitedImmunitySchoolMask` / `limitedAbsorbSchoolMask` (the latter through `saveSchoolMask`) with `schoolShareCoveredBy` and `SCHOOL_SAVE_MIN_SHARE`. Still open: the two windows differ on purpose (a crisis's 2 s vs an attempt's credit window), and — since 2026-10-02 — the KILL ATTEMPTS share also counts the hits a shield ate while cd-hoarded's does not (the 2026-10-02 paragraph below).

**Recorded 2026-10-06 (triage CROSS-THEME G2: cc-dr F-RB1, crisis-external F-K5, sync-burst F-S3)** — the outgoing CC pairing. `analyzeOutgoingCCChains`, `buildCcCategoryHistory` and `analyzeCcBreaks` read the holder's aura stream through `packages/analysis/src/utils/auraIntervals.ts`'s `dropAuraRebroadcasts` (a same-ms REMOVED→APPLIED re-broadcast is one application; ruling A50 = A — since FT-T08, 2026-10-09, up to `AURA_REBROADCAST_GAP_MS` = 1 ms apart, see its row in the index), and a CC never removed closes at `min(round end, apply + officialDurationS)` — the cap `buildAuraIntervals` applies (F-K5; the pairing itself stays separate: a re-APPLIED outgoing CC with no REMOVED is a new DR step, which `buildAuraIntervals`' refresh merge would drop). What ended a CC is `ccTrinketAnalysis.ts`'s `ccRemovalCause` (a logged damage break, the holder's trinket / break press by `castEndedCcWindow` + `breakRemovesCc`, a `SPELL_DISPEL` within `ALLY_DISPEL_MATCH_TOLERANCE_S`); the missed-sync-window `endedBy` fact reads it. **OPEN (F-K5b)**: `healerExposureAnalysis.ts`'s `isEnemyInCC` still replays raw APPLIED / REMOVED events, so a CC never removed stays "in CC" to the round end there (one application in the 60 picks, 69546267's Chastise).

**Recorded 2026-10-06 (triage CROSS-THEME G2: death-kill F-K1 / F-K2 / F-K6)** — KILL ATTEMPTS' kill credit and its softer target. One predicate decides which death a row credits: `extractKillAttempts`' `creditOf` (the target's first death in `[from, min(to, round end) + KILL_CREDIT_SLACK_S]`), and one death credits one row — the row whose `[from, to]` contains it, else the latest-starting one (`killedAtSeconds`). The summary's "outside every attempt window" reads the same credit: a death is outside unless some row's `[from, to]` contains it or it is a `killed` row's `killedAtSeconds` (F-K1), and a burst cluster under a stun attempt is skipped only when it does not reach a death or a covering stun row already credits it (F-K2, ruling A13). F-K6 (ruling A′7 = A): `softerTargetAt` skips an enemy inside one of OUR CC instances (`[CC ON ENEMY]`'s `ccInstances`) of DR category Disorient or Incapacitate (`killAttempts.ts`'s `BREAKABLE_DR_CATEGORIES`) — a DR-category proxy for "damage breaks it" (Cyclone is in the set for a different reason: it cannot be hit). Stuns and roots do not exclude.

**Recorded 2026-10-02 (triage enemy-def F-E22 / F-E24 / F-E7, crisis-external F-A7; Fable review of the KILL ATTEMPTS batch)** — three facts the review moved; the one left OPEN then was closed 2026-10-06. (1) *The school share.* `attributeFailure` reads the TARGET's own record through `incomingPressureBySchool`: landed plus absorbed, every source. The first cut summed the friendly players' `damageOut` — no pet hits — and a shield judged on landed damage alone deletes its own evidence (the better Anti-Magic Shell works, the lower the magic share). An absorbed hit's school is the SPELL_ABSORBED line's own attack-school field (3,849 of 3,849 spell-form absorbs on 4 of the 605 S2 files carry it, equal to DB2's SpellMisc.SchoolMask every time); a swing absorb is physical; a hit's school key is `logSchoolMask` on both sides. Same-side redistribution rows (Spirit Link, Void Leech) are left out by the same rule `incomingPressureEvents` applies (`isRedistributionRow`, roster sides). A window with no damage reads per consumer on purpose: cd-hoarded makes no claim; KILL ATTEMPTS makes no claim for an absorb and still counts an immunity (an immune hit is a MISS line with no amount). **CLOSED 2026-10-06 (user ruling U-KA2: "cd-hoarded 改为与 KA 同口径(含吸收),共用一个谓词")**: cd-hoarded's `dmg2sBySchool` was landed-only — the wall cd-hoarded judges was NOT pressed, so it ate nothing, but another shield on the unit (Power Word: Shield) hid the school it was eating. `crisisDecisionPoints` now fills it from `incomingPressureBySchool` over `dmg2s`'s own window. Measured on the 605 files: cd-hoarded +1 / −0 and 2 lines whose `readyCds` list changes (the 2026-10-02 throwaway variant, on the main of that day, had +1 / 0 / 6). (2) *An external's aura.* `externalAuraOf` is the one cast→aura pairing: the `[ENEMY DEF]` external line's duration, and KILL ATTEMPTS' rule 2 for an external — thrown before the attempt with its aura still on the target when the attempt began → `saved by external (X [up since m:ss])`. A grip / redirect or an instant heal has no aura and counts only inside the span; a school-limited immunity that was merely still up against a go in the other school is no cause (c2058ed4). The aura-only fallback (cast missing from the log) reads `ENEMY_ALLY_SAVE_IDS` too. 2026-10-03 (codex review): the pairing takes the aura from THAT caster, nearest to the cast, and KILL ATTEMPTS reads its externals from the same `[ENEMY DEF]` events — an external seen only as its aura counts where it renders. The save window [from, to] is compared on rendered seconds (`toRenderSecond`), the grid the gate re-parses. (3) *Which immunity lasts its aura.* `immunityLastsItsAura` (may an immunity that was already up count) = the pct-100 table rows plus an immunity-kind aura carrying DB2's all-school immunity (aura 39, mask 127: Time Stop, Guardian of the Forgotten Queen). Burrow, Vanish, Mass Invisibility, Cauterize and Cheat Death mark a moment: damage lands through their auras (605 files: Burrow 80 of 89 auras, Vanish 264 of 533, against Time Stop 1 of 35 and Divine Shield 0 of 408; `fix-KA/immAuraProbe.ts`). **2026-10-06 (user rulings U-KA3 and U-KA3b)**: Burrow, Vanish and Mass Invisibility DO last their aura — `ENEMY_IMMUNITY_HOLDS_ITS_AURA_IDS` (`data/spellIdLists.ts`, registered in `curatedIdRegistry`). The counts above did not tell a DoT tick from a hit, and paired 71 Vanish applications whose REMOVED the log lost with a later removal. Re-measured (`fix-FU/immSplitRaw.py`, same files): Burrow 78 of 89 auras take a periodic tick and 16 any other damage row (60 rows: splash, procs, area damage); Vanish, 462 auras of ≤ 3.5 s, 205 a periodic tick and 123 any other row (273 rows, all in the first 1.5 s: Consecration, Frost / Arcane Splinter, Sun's Avatar, Bladestorm, Frozen Orb). What lands is what was already on the unit or covers the ground under it. Mass Invisibility, 593 auras of ≤ 6.5 s: 99 a periodic tick and 47 any other row, none past the first second — U-KA3b: it counts exactly like Vanish (a periodic tick and damage inside the aura's first second do not deny an immunity), ruled with the 2026-10-01 measurement known (applied to it, the first cut called 250 opening Mass Invisibilities "forced a full immunity" on a target a stun had just landed on). Still a moment: Cauterize (62 of 72 auras take other-than-periodic damage, 47 past the first second), Cheat Death (7 of 10), Feign Death's Survival Tactics (1,135 of 1,474). **User ruling P-FU-b8 (2026-10-06, option C)**: the three ruled-in auras count as "already up" only when the log SAW them end — `immunityCountsWhenAlreadyUp` (KILL ATTEMPTS rule 2) refuses one whose interval is `inferredEnd`. A unit that goes unseen often takes its REMOVED line with it, and `buildAuraIntervals` then closes the aura at its official length: 12 s for Mass Invisibility, where a logged one on an ally ends within 0.6 s (median). Counted at the cap, the 605 files had 313 attempts turn into `forced a full immunity [up since …]`, 293 of them Mass Invisibility and 233 of those rows that count stuns which landed on the "immune" target. A pct-100 table row or a DB2 all-school immunity keeps the cap.

**Recorded 2026-09-30, OPEN (triage H15, ruling A9-3)** — activation as ownership evidence. `extractMajorCooldowns`' ownership filter now counts an aura-backed activation (`auraOnlyActivationSeconds`) like a logged cast, for the `AURA_ACTIVATION_PROVES_BUTTON_IDS` keys only — auras that come from nothing but the press (Feign Death's Survival Tactics 202748, Doom Winds); proc-capable `AURA_ONLY_ACTIVATION_IDS` keys still need a cast. `packages/analysis/src/utils/talentOwnership.ts` → `talentOwnershipOf` (the death-outcome path) still counts SPELL_CAST_SUCCESS only as "cast evidence this round", so a Feign Death seen only through its aura is owned in the ledger and `unknown` / `no` there.
