**Recorded 2026-09-30, closed 2026-10-01 (triage F-H6 × res-readiness F-C3)** — mana affordability. `affordableAt` / `affordableWithin` gate cd-hoarded's accusation set; by the 2026-09-30 ruling (res R2 = A) [RES] `rdy:` keeps an unaffordable cooldown ready and annotates it from `affordableAt` (e.g. `Restoral(no mana 7.0k/11.5k)`) — res F-C3, now in the table above.

**Recorded 2026-09-30, OPEN (triage 2026-09-29 H23)** — the cannot-cast source set. `enemySourceIds` (enemy players + their pets / totems) now feeds the cd-hoarded owner gate, missed-sync-window, the healer cc-avoidable and healer-offense intervals, healing gaps, kick-priority and the missed-cleanse / missed-purge lock tests; burst-window feasibility and `ccTrinketAnalysis` already built the same set inline, and `cdTriggerPrior` uses every non-friendly unit by reaction. Two callers still pass enemy players only: `packages/analysis/src/utils/summonReachability.ts` → `summonReach` (the "free to act" clause on [ENEMY SUMMON]) and `packages/analysis/src/utils/ccTargetState.ts` (the owner-free test behind `ccSamplerFor`). Neither was in the triage's repros; moving them changes context lines, not menus, and needs its own capture.

Same entry, second leg (agy review of that fix): `castBlockingAuraIntervals` still pairs APPLIED / REMOVED itself instead of consuming `packages/analysis/src/utils/auraIntervals.ts` → `buildAuraIntervals` (the authority builder: `spellId:src` keys, a second APPLIED closes the first at the official duration). Two consequences, both pre-existing (the old timestamp pairing had them too): two sources' applications of the same spell that overlap both close at the first REMOVED, so the later stun's tail reads as free; and an application whose REMOVED was never logged pairs with the next application's REMOVED, possibly minutes later. Moving onto `buildAuraIntervals` changes every cannot-cast consumer and needs its own capture. Measured once it had a reader that used to ask `ccInstances` (triage other F-O12, 2026-10-06, 605 files): HEALER OFFENSE's free seconds went down on 794 lines and UP on 6 (+10 s) — each of the 6 a second caster's Hammer of Justice landing on the owner while the first was still up, the later stun's tail read as free. **2026-10-07, first consequence CLOSED (user ruling P-FU-H23)**: `castBlockingAuraIntervals` pairs a removal with ITS caster's application through `packages/analysis/src/utils/drAnalysis.ts` → `matchPendingCcKey` — the pairing `ccInstances` and the CC-break analysis already use (exact `spell:source` key; a BROKEN line carries the breaker, so it falls back to the earliest pending application of the spell) — still in log order, still without the round's clock. 605 files: those 6 free-seconds lines come back down (−10 s); `[SILENCE]` lines 59 fewer (one caster's re-announced silence had printed once per APPLIED) and 15 with a corrected length (two Death Knights' Strangulates: `0s` → `2s`); menu +0 / −3 (one cd-hoarded, one healing-gap, one missed-cleanse whose owner was inside the second stun), 1 cd-hoarded `ownerCc` and one death-setup's `lockedS` 5 → 7. **Still OPEN, the second consequence**: an application whose REMOVED was never logged runs to the same caster's next removal (a 3 s Garrote silence printed as 10 s), and nothing here caps at the official duration — that needs the round's clock in every caller (`buildAuraIntervals`).

**Recorded 2026-09-26, OPEN (reliability round 3 W1a)** — "is this a root". Two layers:

- **"Could this unit move" is unified**: [ROOT] lines, the kick run budget and the crisis DPS "rooted" gate all read `rootIntervalsOf` over the official `data/rootSpells.ts` → `ROOT_SPELL_IDS`.
- **"Does this root count as control" is NOT**: `CONTROL_IDS` (crisis / burst-window responses), burst-window's landed-control check and ccTrinketAnalysis's root windows still read spellTags' `rootSpellIds` (SPELL_CATEGORIES type "roots", 18 ids — a strict subset of the official set, missing 6 of the 24 observed: Ice Nova, Harpoon, Charge's root, Shambling Rush, Immobilized, Entangling Roots 1287975). Aliasing it to the official set was tried on 2026-09-26 and pulled on the capture: a gap-closer's incidental ~1 s root (Charge 105771) displaced a real Shockwave as the "[BURST ANSWERED]" response ("answered with Charge 0.7s before it opened", 3 files), slow-defensive-response −7 / +1, and [RES] cc: filled with "Charge-0s[root]" (1,157 lines). Admitting those ids needs a rule for what counts as a control response (duration floor / not a gap-closer side effect).
  Further open legs, with codex astra's boundary cases:
- **cast → root effect.** `CONTROL_IDS` credits a CAST by its id; a cast whose root is a different aura id (The Hunt 370965 → root 370970) is never a control response. Fix = key casts on the aura they produce (the cast → effect table `data/castEffectAuras.ts`, as the DR view does).
- **burst-window landed-control attribution.** `controlLandedResponses` may backdate a landed aura to any recent untargeted friendly cast, and its `aimed` dedup can suppress a landed root inside the window because a root cast just before `w0` is "aimed" — pre-existing for every CC.
- **ccTrinketAnalysis root windows** are rebuilt by its own apply / remove pairing (APPLIED only, orphan removals dropped) instead of the shared `buildAuraIntervals`.

All three consumers read it — `reconstructEnemyCDTimeline` (and every burst-window consumer downstream), `hasOffensiveSpellActive`/`threatActiveAt`, and the gradient scan's exposure counts. **Empty again as of 2026-08-21.** The dual aura-interval builder registered here on 2026-08-20 (GH #17 burst-into-immunity artifact hunt) is closed: `utils/utils.ts` → `buildFilteredAuraIntervals` is now a thin adapter over `utils/auraIntervals.ts` → `buildAuraIntervals` (see the index row), with the anti-fabrication rules moved up into the authority builder so `aurasActiveAt`/`matchExplore` benefit too.

**Otherwise empty as of 2026-08-01.** The five duplicates recorded when this page was first compiled were all closed the same day; four became shared exports, one turned out not to be a duplicate at all. What was decided:

- **The "healer trained" distance** is now `positionSampling.ts` → `HEALER_TRAINED_YARDS`, imported by the producer and aliased by the gate.
- **"Maximum plausible CC range"** was three numbers claiming to be one fact. It is two facts: `CC_MAX_CAST_RANGE_YARDS` (40 — can the CC reach at all) and `CC_MAX_PLAUSIBLE_RANGE_YARDS` (45 — can this recomputed distance be believed), the second derived from the first so the ordering cannot drift. The gate's private 50 yd is gone: it was looser than the producer's own suppression threshold, so `G6_IMPOSSIBLE_CC` could never fire. Tightening it is behaviour-neutral on today's corpus — of 141237 rendered CC-distance claims, 0 exceed 50 yd and 0 exceed 45 yd (max 44.7).
- **`makeRng`** is imported from `ab/abCompareStats.ts`; the private copy is deleted.
- **`IndexEntry`** is declared once, in `corpus/buildCorpus.ts`, and imported as a type everywhere else including `scripts/positioningScan.ts`.

Not duplicates — recorded so nobody "unifies" them by mistake:

- **"Closest distance in a window" is sampled differently by producer and gate _on purpose_.** `positionAnalysis.ts` walks whole seconds with `INTERP_MAX_GAP_MS` (1500 ms); the gate's `minDistanceInWindow` walks whole seconds _plus_ every advanced-action timestamp _plus_ a sub-second grid, with `LOS_SWEEP_GAP_MS` (3000 ms). The gate's instants are a strict **superset** of the producer's and its gap is looser, and `getUnitPositionAtTime`'s gap only accepts or rejects a sample without changing its value — so `gateMin ≤ producerMin` always holds, and the gate's one-sided test ("claimed closer than physically observed") is the correct expression of that direction, not a workaround. Making the producer adopt the gate's gap would be a regression: `INTERP_MAX_GAP_MS` is the T3 grounding guard that killed fabricated mid-gap interpolation (a false 0.4 yd trained claim). The relationship is pinned end to end in `predicateIndex.test.ts` — the real producer's rendered claim must pass the real gate, with a wrong-window negative control. Only the sampling **instants** are shared, via `positionSampleInstants`.
- **The managed idle-split cadence and the orphan grace window are not the same fact**, though they were both 10 minutes and `ORPHAN_GRACE_MS`'s comment used to say it "mirrors" `IDLE_SPLIT_MS`. `recorder.ts` → `IDLE_SPLIT_MS` bounds how much pre-match lobby footage sits at the head of a match's file (60s since the 2026-09-05 ruling); `recordingsStore.ts` → `ORPHAN_GRACE_MS` (10 min) bounds how long an unclaimed chunk is protected from the orphan cap while its `associate()` message is still in flight. Shortening the cadence only means more orphans sit inside the grace window at once, which is what the window is for — deriving one from the other would silently couple retention safety to a recording-layout preference.
- `HP_AGREEMENT_TOLERANCE_PP` (3 pp) in `promptQualityCheck.ts` is gate-only slack over rendered text. It has no analysis-side counterpart and must not be equated with `HP_SAMPLE_RADIUS_MS`.
- **Two mana samplers, on purpose (2026-09-25, reliability audit D2).** The context lines read `manaReadingAt` (nearest mana-bearing sample within the HP radius). The raw-stream `manaAt` holds the last reading at or before t with no bound; its consumers are the retired mana-pressure / mana-efficiency candidates (OOM-window bridging needs exactly that hold-last-value) and `matchExplore`. Unifying them would change either the bridging or the rendered lines.
- `quality/coverageManifest.ts` deliberately refuses to share the analysis pipeline: sharing it would make the check circular. It shares only static tables (`ccSpellIds`, `trinketSpellIds`, `getEnglishSpellName`, `specToString`).

**Recorded 2026-10-11, OPEN (FT leftovers; nothing built — needs a design)** — when a pet is gone. The cooldown and kit readers treat a pet's abilities as available for the whole round; no reader asks whether the pet is alive. What the raw log offers, read on five new-season files (142 `Pet-` GUIDs; probe `n7_pet_end_rows_raw.py` in the eval-private fix-FT scripts): (1) a permanent pet's death IS logged — `UNIT_DIED` with the pet's GUID as destination (3 rows, all in e0e45175: a hunter pet died three times), and a damage row with overkill > 0 on it (4 rows in that file); totems and guardians are the opposite case (`nonPlayerUnitKill` in `timelineHelpers.ts`: overkill is nearly their only evidence). (2) A pet that comes back is a NEW GUID: the owner's `SPELL_SUMMON` row (Revive Pet 982, Call Pet 1–5, Raise Dead 52150, the warlock summons) names it, and it differs from the dead one in the spawn counter that opens the GUID's last segment (`…-165189-0204BBD685` → `…-165189-0304BBD685`, same pet name). So "the pet is back" is a summon row of the same owner, not the old GUID acting again. (3) Rows with the dead GUID as SOURCE keep coming after its `UNIT_DIED` (3 of 3: running periodic effects), so a later source row is not evidence of life. (4) Dismiss Pet 2641 is a cast row of the owner with no row on the pet at all; a dismissed or despawned pet (owner's death, stable swap, out of range) writes nothing — 12.x has no despawn event (docs/log-observability-audit.md, direction 4). A design has to say which of these end a pet's abilities (death certainly; dismissal only through the owner's cast), what an unknown end reads as, and that a kit line may then change — candidate rows keyed on a pet ability being ready can move.

**Recorded 2026-10-11, OPEN (FT leftovers, the chained-cast item)** — a cast's SPELL_CAST_SUCCESS logged at the next cast bar's START. Every reader ties a SUCCESS row to a bar by time alone (`castCancels.ts` `ownerCastBarOutcomes`, `kickAudit.ts` `openCastOf`: `timestamp >= start`; the log has no cast GUID). Read on the raw rows of five files (probe `n7_chained_casts.py` in the eval-private fix-FT scripts, every unit): a SUCCESS within a few ms of a START of the same spell is one of two things, and the row ORDER tells them apart. (a) The SUCCESS row follows the START row — the cast went off at once (a proc made it instant; the client still writes a START): 28 of the recorders' 245 bars, 589 of the other players' 1,276. The bar completed and the readers are right. (b) The SUCCESS row precedes the START row at the same timestamp — it is the PREVIOUS cast's end, written together with the next bar's start: 0 of the recorders' 245 bars, 16 of the other players' 1,276 (4 of them with no other SUCCESS in the bar's window), 651 of the 1,272 bars of non-player units (treants and other guardians, which no reader reads). So for the recorder — the only input of `ownerCastBarOutcomes` — the reported misreading was not found (the product's own reading agrees: 10 files, 418 recorder bars, 0 SUCCESS rows shared by two bars, 0 bars `completed` inside `CAST_QUEUE_TOLERANCE_MS` of their START with an interruption row or a kick after it, probe `n7_chainedBars.ts`), and `[CAST STOPPED]` and the cancel ledger were left as they are. Case (b) on another player reaches `openCastOf` (the juke test: an enemy cast "never finished"): a stopped bar whose window holds only the previous cast's SUCCESS is not open to it, so a kick into it reads a plain miss rather than `JUKED by fake`. Not changed here: it moves what "juked" counts, a classification candidate rows read. The rule that would close it needs no threshold — a row whose `logLine.lineIndex` is below the START's was logged before the bar began and cannot be its end (old archives carry no `lineIndex` and would read as today).

On a CJK client `checkCjkLeak` fails such a line; on a French, German, Spanish or Portuguese client the localized name passes it unseen. Not changed: the log does not say which locale wrote it, and the six were in none of the five files read. **Recorded 2026-10-11, measured, unchanged (FT leftovers)** — `AURA_BEFORE_CAST_MAX_S` (50 ms, `enemyDefensives.ts`) against the note that Dark Pact's aura was once seen 58 ms before its cast row. **Recorded 2026-10-11, OPEN (re-eval I05, option c)** — "does a stun stop THIS button". Three readers now answer it with `usableWhileStunned`, each over its own span: the `[DEATH]` `Unused:` list (`wasLockedOutByStunOnly` over the lethal window, all-or-nothing: one non-stun CC in the window and the table is not consulted), `cheaper available:` (`ownerStunnedAtCast`, the stuns at the press) and — since I05 — cd-hoarded's owner gate and `ownerFreeS` (`stunLetsPress`, per interval, through `actWindowFor`'s `stunPressable`). Every other reader that asks about a named spell still takes a stun as stopping it, because `intervalBlocksSpell` / `cannotCastIntervalsForSpells` do: the sync-window ready gate and `holderCc`, missed-purge / missed-cleanse "locked", the kick run budget, cc-avoidable, `[CD PRIOR]`'s castable seconds, burst-window feasibility, the death block's option tags (`[DEFENSIVE AVAILABLE]` "free to press it"). The direction there is the exemption's (a stunned holder is never accused), so none of them is wrong against the player; moving the reading into `intervalBlocksSpell` would ADD accusations in each and needs its own ruling and capture per reader. Not modelled anywhere: the feared / confused dimensions of the same table (`USABLE_WHILE_FEARED_SPELL_IDS`, `USABLE_WHILE_CONFUSED_SPELL_IDS` — cc-avoidable alone reads them), and whether a silence stops a cooldown (`isSilenceableCast` is read by `castBlockingAuraAt` only).

## Keeping this page honest

`packages/eval/test/predicateIndex.test.ts` is the executable half of this page. It

- imports every predicate listed above by its file path and fails if any is missing or renamed;
- parses the table out of both language versions and fails if they list different predicates, or if either disagrees with the test's own list;
- asserts the pairs that cannot share an export: that the gate's LoS tolerances, CC cap and trained distance are still _derived_ from the analysis exports rather than re-typed as literals, that `matchDateKey` still formats through `dateKeyOf`, that the report curve's `METRIC_BASES` still composes each metric the way the leaderboard's `meterValue` does (Healing counts absorbs on both sides), and that `eventInRange` and `msInRange` still agree on both inclusive bounds;
- asserts that `makeRng` and `IndexEntry` each have exactly one declaration in the whole `packages/eval` tree — the only way to pin a type, which the compiler erases;
- asserts the producer/gate inverses end to end — a window rendered through `fmtTime` + `renderedWindowSeconds` passes `checkWindowSpanConsistency`, percentiles taken from `toSortedFinite` pass `checkPercentileMonotonicity`, and a `HEALER_TRAINED` claim produced by the real `computeOwnerPositionEvents` and rendered by the real formatter passes the real gate — each with a negative control, so the assertion cannot pass vacuously.

Run it with `npm test --workspace=packages/eval`.
